name: Jakobskreuz Buchensteinwand
kurzbeschreibung: The Jakobskreuz on the 1,456 m high Buchensteinwand in the Pillerseetal: at 30 m tall, the world's largest accessible summit cross featuring four viewing platforms.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Jakobskreuz towers on the 1,456-metre summit of the Buchensteinwand in the Tyrolean Pillerseetal (district of Kitzbühel) and stands as a widely visible architectural landmark of the Kitzbüheler Alpen. With an overall height of almost 30 metres, the imposing double cross is the largest accessible summit cross in the world. Erected in honour of Saint James – the patron saint of the historic pilgrimage route Jakobsweg Tirol that runs through the valley –, the monument unites spiritual pilgrimage traditions with cutting-edge wood and steel architecture. From the four projecting viewing arms, a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic view opens up over the Kitzbühel mountains, the snow-covered Hohe Tauern, and the rugged limestone massifs of the Wilder Kaiser as well as the Loferer und Leoganger Steinberge.

Architecture & Viewing Platforms

The ceremonial inauguration of this major project took place in July 2014 following roughly two years of planning and construction. The daring design is based on a massive steel and reinforced concrete core, harmoniously clad on the exterior with local larch wood. Inside the structure, a modern glazed passenger lift and a panoramic staircase provide access to the various floors. At a height of about 19 metres, the building's four cross-shaped arms branch out in all four cardinal directions: each arm houses a fully glazed, weather-protected exhibition and seminar room, each fronted by an open-air observation gallery. The rooms are used year-round for rotating art exhibitions by regional Tyrolean artists, spiritual meditations, and cultural events. The ultimate highlight is the uppermost roof terrace at nearly 30 metres: equipped with panorama panels and telescopes, it offers an incomparable downward vista over the Pillerseetal and the emerald-green waters of the Pillersee. Around the cross, the family-friendly Blumen- und Sagenweg Buchensteinwand thematic trail was created.

Visit & Getting There

The Jakobskreuz is open daily during the summer and winter seasons of the Bergbahnen Pillersee from 09:00 to 16:45 (summer operations usually run from mid-May to late October). Admission to the Jakobskreuz is available separately or as a discounted combined ticket with the mountain lift. Fares for ascent and descent including Jakobskreuz admission (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €29.00, seniors approx. €26.00, children (born 2009–2018) approx. €15.00; admission to the cross alone (for hikers) approx. €9.50. Significant discounts apply with the regional PillerseeTal Card or the Kitzbüheler Alpen Sommer Card. Arrival by cable car: The comfortable 4-seater chairlift of the Bergbahn Pillersee starts in St. Jakob in Haus and carries visitors directly to the summit in around 12 minutes. For mountain hikers, well-marked hiking trails lead up from St. Ulrich, St. Jakob, or Fieberbrunn in about 1.5 to 2 hours. By car: Via the B164 to Fieberbrunn or St. Jakob in Haus to the large free car park at the Buchensteinwand valley station. By public transport: ÖBB trains to Hochfilzen or Fieberbrunn station, from where the regional Pillerseetal regional bus runs directly to the cable car.

Tips

Thanks to the modern chairlift and the integrated passenger elevator inside the cross, the entire Jakobskreuz is fully barrier-free and wheelchair-accessible for visitors with reduced mobility as well as families with prams. Directly at the base of the cross, the Berggasthof Buchensteinwand with its large sun terrace invites you to enjoy Tyrolean culinary specialities. Visit the cross in the morning on a clear day to capture the rugged rocky peaks of the Loferer Steinberge in ideal photographic light.
